artists.biography:
Crippled Black Phoenix is a rock supergroup from the United Kingdom. Several musicians have contributed to Crippled Black Phoenix's albums and play with them during their live shows.

Members of the band used to play in other bands (including Iron Monkey, Gonga, Mogwai, Electric Wizard and others). In 2004, Justin Greaves began recording primitive sounds he had in mind for years. He was encouraged by Dominic Aitchison, and their ideas would lay the backbone for Crippled Black Phoenix.
Although originally having an unorthodox start, since all the band members were part of and busy with other projects at the time of the band's founding, Crippled Black Phoenix remained committed to staying together and forged their sound. The band writes what they call "endtime ballads," signifying both the slightly macabre nature of their songs and their unusual blend of styles as the final evolution in music. This blend has led to them being called everything from stoner-prog to freak-folk to doom.

Crippled Black Phoenix have made live shows a focus and have performed in unusual venues, using Victorian-era instruments in tandem with more modern instruments.

perplexity.description:
No Sadness Or Farewell, released in 2012 by Crippled Black Phoenix on Cool Green Recordings, is a studio album that showcases the band’s signature blend of dark rock, psychedelic, and progressive elements. Led by Justin Greaves, the album features a rich tapestry of instrumentation, including guitars, keyboards, electronics, and occasional banjo, layered with atmospheric textures and dynamic shifts. The music ranges from heavy, guitar-driven passages to quieter, introspective moments, drawing comparisons to artists like David Bowie and Magazine while maintaining a distinct, brooding identity. Tracks such as “Jonestown Martin” and “Long Live Independence” exemplify the band’s ability to merge powerful rock with experimental flourishes.

Within Crippled Black Phoenix’s discography, No Sadness Or Farewell follows the ambitious double album Mankind (The Crafty Ape) and continues the band’s evolution toward a more expansive and genre-defying sound. The album is recognized for its emotional depth and sonic diversity, marking a high point in their early period. Critics have praised its ambitious arrangements and genre-blending approach, with some noting its unique mix of melancholy and intensity. While not a mainstream commercial breakthrough, the album solidified Crippled Black Phoenix’s reputation among fans of progressive and alternative rock, earning positive reviews for its creativity and musicianship.
